newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yields fall on three, six, 12-month Yemen t-bills.
newsitem.headline: Yields fall on three, six, 12-month Yemen t-bills.

text.p: The Central Bank of Yemen said yields fell on the two billion rials worth of three-month, six-month and 12-month treasury bills on offer at its latest tender.
The Bank said its 91-day treasury bills issued on Saturday yielded an average 13.49 percent, down from the average 17.95 percent at the May 10 auction.
Of the one billion rials worth of bills on offer, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 950 million rials.
The average price was 9,674.51 rials and the lowest price accepted was 9,651.10 rials. Yields ranged between 11.98 percent and 14.50 percent.

The latest issue of 182-day bills yielded an average 13.23 percent from 18.21 percent at the previous auction. Of the 600 million rials worth of bills on offer, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 570 million rials.
The average price was 9,381.24 rials and the lowest price accepted was 9,331.16 rials. Yields ranged from 9.49 percent to 14.38 percent.
The latest issue of 364-day bills yielded an average 13.59 percent from 18.43 percent at the May 10 auction.

Of the 400 million rials of 364-day bills on offer, the issue attracted bids totalling 380 million rials. The average price was 8,806.65 rials and the lowest price accepted was 8,736.65 rials. Yields ranged from 12.02 to 14.50 percent.
